This page describes the package-specific multi-trait annotation-informed
mixture formulation implemented by `sblr`. It should not be read as a claim of
exact equivalence to a separately published BayesRC implementation.

## Public models and state space

`mtblr_bed(method = "bayesrc")` is individual-level;
`mtblr_csr(method = "sbayesrc")` and
`mtblr_block_eigen(method = "sbayesrc")` are summary-statistics routes. All
use `prior_kernel = "bayesrc"` and the same unique-null, non-null
trait-pattern by positive-component state space described for
[MT BayesR](mt_bayesr_sbayesr.qmd).

## Factorized annotation prior

Let $A_j$ be marker $j$'s processed annotation row and let

$$
\theta_{jc}=P(c_j=c\mid A_j),\qquad c=0,\ldots,K,
$$

be annotation-dependent component probabilities from probit stick breaking.
Let

$$
\omega_p=P(a_j=p\mid c_j>0),\qquad p=1,\ldots,P,
$$

be global conditional probabilities for the supplied non-null trait patterns.
The complete state prior is

$$
P(\text{null}\mid A_j)=\theta_{j0},
$$

$$
P(a_j=p,c_j=k\mid A_j)=\theta_{jk}\omega_p,\qquad k>0.
$$

Both simplexes sum to one, so this factorization preserves one null state. It
does not fit annotation-dependent trait-pattern probabilities.

## Annotation alignment and preprocessing

`annotations` must be a finite numeric matrix or data frame with unique,
nonempty column names and exact marker identity. External annotations require
unique marker row names; exact identifier matching may reorder rows, but the
implementation never intersects or silently drops markers.

Preprocessing happens once per fit and records original/processed names,
column types, centers, scales, intercept policy, and marker-alignment status.
An existing intercept is preserved; `add_intercept = TRUE` adds at most one.
Eligible continuous columns are standardized when requested. Binary columns
follow the explicit `center_binary_annotations` policy. Constant or nonfinite
columns fail according to the preprocessing contract. The caller's matrix is
not modified.

## Probit stick breaking

For $K+1$ categories (null plus $K$ positive components), the coefficient
matrix has processed annotations in rows and deterministic sticks in columns.
Stick order follows component order. Linear predictors are transformed by the
normal CDF, floored only by `pi_floor`, and renormalized.

`alpha_init` and `sigmaSqAlpha_init` initialize coefficients and their
positive prior variances. `intercept_flat` distinguishes the intercept prior.
With `updateAlpha = TRUE`, latent probit variables, coefficients, and
`sigmaSqAlpha` are updated every `alpha_update_every` completed iterations;
the current values still exist at every iteration. With `FALSE`, coefficients
remain fixed. `updatePi` separately controls the conditional pattern
probabilities $\omega$.

## Effects and independent MAF scaling

Conditional on a selected state, the effect prior is unchanged from MT
BayesR:

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\beta_{j,p,k})=
\gamma_k q_j(S)B_p.
$$

Annotations change component probabilities only. They do not change $B$,
the residual covariance, component multipliers, operators, or the optional
`maf_effect_s` scale. Fixed MT `maf_effect_s` is supported; sampled MT
`maf_effect_s` is not. When an explicitly identified MAF/heterozygosity
annotation is combined with `maf_effect_s`, the fit records the overlap and
warns once because both mechanisms may encode related information.

## Probability outputs

- `prior_component_probabilities`: posterior mean annotation-driven prior
  probabilities $\theta_j$, marker by component;
- `prior_active_probabilities`: $1-\theta_{j0}$;
- `component_probabilities`: posterior marker component-state probabilities;
- `pattern_pi_final`, `pattern_pi_mean`, `pattern_pi_trace`: the conditional
  non-null pattern probabilities $\omega$;
- annotation coefficient and variance final/mean fields: the probit-stick
  parameter summaries.

Because the component prior is marker dependent, `pi_final`, `pi_mean`, and
`pi_trace` are present but `NULL`; they are not redefined as marker-averaged
probabilities. Model-specific quantities live under
`model_parameters$annotations`.

## Limitations and identifiability

- Trait-pattern probabilities are global conditional on non-null status.
- Annotations do not modify covariance matrices or component scales.
- Sampled MT `maf_effect_s` is unsupported.
- MAF-derived annotations and `maf_effect_s` can overlap or be confounded.
- Annotation coefficients diagnose component propensity, not causal
  enrichment by themselves.
- The current factorization is the model implemented by `sblr`, not a claim of
  a universally standardized external MT BayesRC definition.

See [Annotation-informed models](../notes/annotation_informed_models.qmd) for
practical selection and [Annotation priors](annotation_priors.qmd) for broader
prior context.
